cands.name: Allison T Montgomery

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Huntsville native and software engineer supporting Redstone Arsenal. She has a UAH computer engineering degree and says she has done grassroots advocacy at the Alabama State House for several years. She has not held public office. Democratic nominee for House District 25.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists her as recommended by four Sway voter-guide groups: Birds of a Feather Vote Together, Tabitha's List, Unburdening The Ballot, and YALLvote.

cands.gaps: We could not find any record of her holding public office, so there are no deeds in office to report. Her campaign platform page was cut off, so some of her stated positions may be missing. We found nothing on her views on homestead property taxes, land ownership by investors or foreigners, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B visas, policing, gun laws, or abortion. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. Her education, work history and advocacy experience come from her own campaign site and were not independently confirmed.

cands.name: Phillip K. Rigsby

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Huntsville pharmacist and business owner. He owns Huntsville Compounding Pharmacy and The Medicine Shoppe Pharmacy. He earned a Doctor of Pharmacy from Auburn University in 2000. He was a Republican member of the Alabama House for District 25 from November 2022 to 2026.
cands.gaps: We found no documented stances from him on data centers, development, property taxes, immigration, guns, abortion or school choice. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022 or 2026. His campaign site says he helped pass price transparency for prescription drugs, a halving of the grocery tax, and $1.5 billion in taxpayer savings. We did not find bill records to confirm these claims or his role in them. Ballotpedia's list of bills he sponsored did not load, so we can't say what he sponsored. Ballotpedia found no endorsements for him in 2026. We found no controversies or foreign ties in the pages available. We did not find when, if ever, he lived outside Alabama.
